Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Attached is the SOW and a first-pass CSV with the usage dimensions our billing team tracks. High-level: we sell monthly subscriptions by seat (Seats), API calls (APIUnits), and a premium feature add-on (FeatureX-hours). We need the Marketplace metering to support pro-rated seat changes and a consumption SKU for APIUnits.

Can Redwood map those to Product Codes and set up fulfillment testing in the AWS sandbox? We have an internal deadline to go-live with Marketplace fulfillment by 2027-04-21.

Best,
Lena
Product Ops, DataWave Analytics

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@datawave.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff - AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment

Quick read of the CSV — overall looks straightforward. Notes:
- Seats => map to subscription SKU (metering by quantity). Proration supported by AWS via entitlement updates but we need to surface delta events from DataWave at daily cadence.
- APIUnits => consumption SKU. Need to confirm whether DataWave will report cumulative usage (preferred) or delta events. Our ingestion prefers cumulative usage with a timestamp.
- FeatureX-hours => could be either a separate metered SKU or bundled as quantity; recommend separate metered SKU to avoid pricing skew.

I'll draft the mapping table and include expected API payloads for Marketplace Metering/Entitlement. Priyom, do you want me to push a sample CSV into the Redwood S3 test bucket for you to run ingestion tests?

Ben
Enterprise Sales Engineer

---

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@datawave.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff - AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment

Thanks — I pulled the CSV from the S3 link Ben provided and started a run in the sandbox. Early findings:
- The CSV columns map cleanly to our ingestion pipeline except one: "FeatureX-hours" uses fractional hours (e.g., 1.5). AWS metering prefers integer units. We can multiply by 60 and report minutes as integer units, but that requires update to DataWave's exporter.
- Seat proration test: I simulated a mid-cycle seat decrease and observed the entitlement delta flows correctly, but AWS sandbox returned a 409 on one of the entitlement revocations. I'll open a support ticket with AWS Marketplace Support and paste the case id here.

Test plan (short):
1) Push mapped CSV to Redwood test S3 bucket (ben will upload).
2) Redwood ingest -> map to product codes -> send metering events to AWS sandbox.
3) Validate billing report in DataWave sandbox account and confirm proration handling.
4) Run failure/retry scenarios (network errors, duplicate events).

ETA for test completion: 2027-04-06 if we get the small exporter change from DataWave by 2027-04-01.

Priyom
Marketplace Integrations

---

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Quick billing note: we can support prorated seat credits but need to surface two things to DataWave's billing system: (1) the effective change timestamp, and (2) the original seat count for reconciliation. We'll provide a reconciliation CSV template.

I'll attach the template and the sample invoice mapping in a follow-up email and will work with Accounting to ensure settlement timelines align with DataWave's finance calendar.

Next steps summary:
- Ben to upload sample mapping CSV to Redwood test bucket (today).
- Priyom to complete sandbox run and open AWS support ticket for 409 case (Priyom to paste ID here once created).
- Lena/DataWave: update exporter for FeatureX to report minutes or confirm alternate mapping by 2027-04-01.
- Karthik/legal: route SOW for signature; I flagged billing appendix items that require sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Billing Ops Lead
Redwood Inference
